info.title: MyBricks API
info.description:
The back-end of **MyBricks**, a real-estate portfolio manager.

**Authentication.** Sign-in, sign-up, guest mode, invitations and the admin plugin are served by Better Auth under `/api/auth/*` (see its own reference at `/api/auth/reference`). They set a session cookie; every other endpoint reads it. The organization a request works in comes from the session, never from the client.

**Conventions.**
- Money is always an integer number of **cents** (BRL). Rates, yields and the IRR are fractions (`0.07` is 7%), except where a field says "percent".
- Calendar dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps are ISO 8601.
- Lists are paginated: `?page=1&pageSize=20` (at most 100) and answer `{ items, page, pageSize, total }`.
- Errors always look like `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`.
- **Visibility.** Owners and admins see every record of the organization; members only the ones they created. Something outside what the caller may see answers `404`, never `403`, so ids of other people's records do not leak.

get.description: One-off or monthly-recurring revenues and expenses that are not rent. With `from` / `to`, recurring transactions are kept when their monthly occurrences touch the period (the end date counts by month, inclusive), not only when `occurredOn` is inside it.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the period (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). Together with `to` it keeps one-off transactions whose `occurredOn` is inside the period, and recurring ones whose monthly occurrences touch it: they started on or before `to` and have no end date or end in the month of `from` or later (the end counts by month, inclusive, as in the IRR).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the period (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). See `from`.

get.description:
Revenue and expenses month by month for a window of up to 36 months (`from` and `to` as YYYY-MM, both included; empty months come back as zeros). Calculated on every request, so a recurring transaction, which is one record, is expanded here instead of in the client. Everything is in integer cents.

**Revenue.** `rentCents` is the rent in force in the month, with the same source the indicators use (the rent typed on the property in manual mode, the conventional contract in contract mode) times the expected occupancy rate; a contract counts from its first to its last month, both included, and a replacement wins the month it starts. Short-stay properties earn from bookings instead: `reservationsCents` takes the confirmed reservations whose check-in is in the month, in full (they are not spread over the nights). `transactionsCents` takes the revenue transactions: one-off ones in the month they occurred and recurring ones in every month from the first until the month of the end (inclusive, or without end), the same reading the IRR and the transactions period filter use.

**Expenses.** `fixedCents` is the annual expenses of the property divided by 12; `transactionsCents` are the expense transactions, with the same month rules.

**Own use and loan for use** produce no income. Without `propertyId` they are left out entirely (no rent, bookings, fixed expenses or transactions), exactly as `/api/kpis/portfolio` leaves them out of the portfolio income and expenses. With `propertyId` the property is shown as it is: no rent or bookings, but its fixed expenses and transactions still count, as in `/api/kpis/properties/{id}`.

**Ownership.** Without `propertyId`, the amounts of each property are weighted by its ownership percentage before being added, like `/api/kpis/portfolio`. With `propertyId`, the values are those of the whole property, like `/api/kpis/properties/{id}`.

**Financing.** The financing schedule is not added automatically: an installment is already a transaction (category "Parcela de financiamento") when the owner records it, and adding both would count it twice.

Members only see the properties they created.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last month of the window (YYYY-MM), included. The window has at most 36 months

parameters.name: propertyId
parameters.description: Only this property, as a whole (not weighted by ownership share). Without it: the whole portfolio the caller can see, weighted by ownership share
